@c1-ease/card is a dependency-confusion package: its description is "Compatibility shim." and its README calls it an "authorized dependency-confusion test" by "Kero (@0xWise)". Each listed version has a postinstall script that runs `node beacon.cjs` on npm install, and index.js runs the same code when the package is imported; it POSTs the hostname, install path and current working directory to `https://vmi3699893.contaboserver.net:8787/_ah/dc` with TLS certificate checks turned off, and index.js exports a Proxy of no-op functions so builds that import the real package keep running. The npm account ppblpp1 published @c1-ease/card and 7 other packages with the same beacon on 2026-11-21 between 21:34 and 22:09 UTC.

## Source: amazon-inspector (cf1ed7404d29e131f0f3008773ffedf222e2df2d27753bd0e35655762dfc5821)
The package publishes under the scoped name `@c1-ease/card` with no legitimate functionality: `index.js` exports a Proxy that returns a no-op function for any property access, allowing a victim build that resolves this public package instead of an internal `@c1-ease/*` dependency to continue without crashing. `package.json` declares a `postinstall` hook that runs `node beacon.cjs`, and the same beacon is invoked on `require()` of the module. `beacon.cjs` collects host identifiers — `os.hostname()`, `__dirname` (install path), `process.cwd()`, and `process.version` — and POSTs them as JSON to the hardcoded endpoint `https://vmi3699893.contaboserver.net:8787/_ah/dc`, with TLS certificate validation explicitly disabled via `rejectUnauthorized: false`. The combination of a scoped-namespace squat shim, an install-time and import-time outbound beacon to a third-party Contabo VPS, and disabled TLS validation is the standard dependency-confusion exfiltration shape.
